system_description.narrative_title: Global bond-market sell-off and rising yields
system_description.narrative_summary: A synchronized global sell-off in sovereign and fixed-income markets — driven by rising inflation fears (fueled by higher oil and gas prices and Middle East tensions), stronger economic data, and central-bank repricing — has pushed yields to multi-year highs. That rise in yields is feeding back into currencies, equity valuations and sovereign borrowing costs, forcing responses from central banks and governments and raising contagion and fiscal-stress risks across markets.
system_description.scope: Sovereign and corporate bond markets (yields, curves, spreads), investor flows into/out of bond funds, central-bank policy signalling and rate expectations, inflation drivers (oil/gas, wages, services prices), currency moves, and immediate market reactions in equities, gold and credit
system_description.super_system: Global financial system and macroeconomy (cross-border capital flows, monetary policy, fiscal solvency and global trade/commodity dynamics)
adjacent_subsystems: Energy markets (oil, gas) influencing inflation expectations
Fiscal policy and sovereign debt management
Central bank policy coordination and communications (Fed, ECB, BOJ)
Equity and corporate credit markets (valuations, funding conditions)

variables.name: Nominal long-term yield
variables.description: The prevailing level of long-term sovereign bond yields (eg, 10-year) aggregated across markets, measured as a continuously varying interest-rate level.

variables.name: Short-term policy rate expectations
variables.description: Market-implied expected short-term policy interest rate path over the near to medium term, as it evolves with new information.

variables.name: Term premium
variables.description: The component of long-term yields that compensates investors for interest-rate and reinvestment risk over and above expected short rates.

variables.name: Sovereign and corporate credit spreads
variables.description: The additional yield over risk-free benchmarks demanded for sovereign and corporate credit, aggregated across markets and maturities.

variables.name: Market inflation expectations
variables.description: Forward-looking inflation expectations priced into financial markets for various horizons, expressed as continuously varying rates.

variables.name: Realized headline inflation rate
variables.description: The observed current headline inflation rate (eg, CPI-type measure) that changes continuously as new price data are recorded.

variables.name: Energy price level
variables.description: Aggregate oil and gas price level (per unit), representing commodity-price pressure that feeds into broader inflation dynamics.

variables.name: Wage growth rate
variables.description: The rate of nominal wage increases across the economy, which continuously influences cost pressures and inflation persistence.

variables.name: Services-price inflation rate
variables.description: The inflation rate for services-sector prices, capturing the non-tradable component of inflation that tends to be sticky.

variables.name: Market liquidity in bond markets
variables.description: The depth, bid-ask tightness and ease of transacting in sovereign and corporate bonds, measured as a continuously varying liquidity state.

variables.name: Cross-border capital flow rate
variables.description: The net rate of capital moving across borders into or out of fixed-income assets, measured per unit time and varying continuously.

variables.name: Net flows into bond funds
variables.description: Net purchases or redemptions into bond mutual funds and ETFs per unit time, representing investor allocation flows to fixed income.

variables.name: Bond-market volatility
variables.description: Short-term realized and implied volatility in fixed-income markets, reflecting the variability of bond prices and yields over time.

variables.name: Currency strength index
variables.description: A continuous index of major-currency values and directional pressure relative to peers, capturing exchange-rate-driven valuation shifts.

variables.name: Fiscal financing gap
variables.description: Aggregate government primary deficit and gross borrowing need relative to available financing capacity, represented as a continuously varying gap.

variables.name: Investor risk appetite
variables.description: The prevailing willingness of investors to accept risk (hold riskier assets versus safe assets), captured as a continuously varying sentiment state.

catalysts.title: Federal Reserve September meeting and guidance
catalysts.description: FOMC decision and accompanying guidance in September will reset market-implied policy path and influence yields and risk sentiment.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines note Fed officials (Waller/Williams) and a September meeting could alter rate expectations (e.g. 'Fed Governor Waller indicates he will support holding rates steady at September meeting').

catalysts.title: Bank of Japan September rate repricing
catalysts.description: BOJ signals and likely September moves that further tighten policy or signal higher rates, repricing global short-rate expectations and FX.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'BOJ chief signals chance of September rate hike' and 'Bank of Japan’s Ueda vows to keep raising interest rates.'

catalysts.title: Ongoing oil and European gas price surge (Middle East tensions)
catalysts.description: Escalating Middle East tensions and Europe gas tightness sustain upward pressure on oil and gas prices, feeding inflation expectations and yields.
catalysts.rationale: Multiple headlines link oil/gas surge and Mideast turmoil to bond sell-off (e.g. 'Energy price surge hits bond markets', 'Global Bond Yields Surge as Oil Prices Fuel Inflation Worries').

catalysts.title: Continued net inflows into bond funds
catalysts.description: Ongoing investor purchases of bond funds despite rising yields could absorb supply and temper further yield rises.
catalysts.rationale: Headline: 'Rising yields aren’t scaring off investors. Why money is still pouring into bond funds.'

catalysts.title: Fed officials' communications ahead of policy meeting
catalysts.description: Ongoing public comments from Fed officials will continue to shift market rate expectations and volatility before the FOMC decision.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines highlight Waller and Williams remarks moving yields and sentiment (e.g. 'Fed Governor Waller indicates he will support holding rates steady', 'Fed’s Williams “is opening options”').

catalysts.title: Emerging-market credit stress from higher global yields
catalysts.description: Sustained higher global yields strain EM borrowing costs and capital flows, widening sovereign and corporate spreads and pressuring fiscal gaps.
catalysts.rationale: IMF and news warn rising yields threaten developing-country debt and bailouts (e.g. 'IMF's Georgieva says rising bond yields threaten progress', 'IMF agrees $2.2bn bailout for Senegal').

catalysts.title: Potential BOJ/finance ministry FX intervention to curb yen moves
catalysts.description: Heightened yen moves could prompt intervention, which would quickly affect currency and cross-border flows and jitter bond markets.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines note 'intervention chatter' and 'Yen jumps as traders bet on Japan interest rate rises', implying intervention risk.

catalysts.title: ECB policy guidance and rate path
catalysts.description: ECB officials' hawkish signals or a decision to lift rates further will affect euro-area yields, spreads and global rate expectations.
catalysts.rationale: Headlines: 'ECB must be prepared to lift interest rates further' and damage to French government bonds from hawkish ECB remarks.
